st.3: It was discovered in 1954 and excavated in 1955–60 by S.R. Rao.

x: All four statements are correct: Lothal on the Bhogava has the earliest tidal dock (about 218 m × 37 m), and it was discovered and excavated by S.R. Rao.

st.2: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837 with the help of bilingual Indo-Greek coins.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Prinsep read Brahmi (1837) from the Ashokan inscriptions; bilingual Indo-Greek coins were the key to Kharosthi.

st.3: Ekarat in the Aitareya Brahmana means a ruler elected by the Samiti.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ekarat means the sole or paramount ruler, not an elected one.

st.3: The first mention of the Andhras is not in it but in the Aitareya Brahmana.

x: All three statements are correct: the Shatapatha is the largest Brahmana, tells the Flood story and the eastward journey of Videgha Madhava, while the Andhras are first mentioned in the Aitareya Brahmana.
Both statements are correct: the Gopatha Brahmana and the Mundaka Upanishad (like the Mandukya and Prashna) belong to the Atharvaveda.

st.3: The Avestan parallel of Rita is Haoma.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Avestan parallel of Rita is Asha; Haoma is the parallel of Soma.

st.3: Ghantasala (Kantakasala) was the inland capital of the Ikshvakus.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ghantasala (Kantakasala) in Krishna district was an ancient port; the Ikshvaku capital was Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda).

st.2: Mauryan punch-marked coins were mainly of gold.
st.4: The Milindapanho is a Mauryan source on the reign of Bindusara.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Mauryan punch-marked coins were mainly of silver. Statement 4 is wrong: the Milindapanho is a dialogue of the Indo-Greek king Menander with Nagasena, not a Mauryan source.

st.2: Vasudeva Kanva, a minister, founded the dynasty that directly followed the Mauryas.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mauryas were directly followed by the Shungas of Pushyamitra; Vasudeva Kanva later overthrew the last Shunga.

st.2: Kautilya lists nine kinds of dasas.

x: All four statements are correct: Megasthenes saw no slaves, but Kautilya lists nine kinds of dasas, bars making an Arya a slave and gives the slave woman's son by her master the status of the master's son.

st.2: They were dedicated to the Ajivikas by Ashoka himself.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Nagarjuni caves were given to the Ajivikas by Ashoka's grandson Dasaratha; Ashoka gave the nearby Barabar caves.

st.3: The nivartana, the land measure of Satavahana grants, was used for grants made only to Brahmanas, never to Buddhist monks.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the nivartana (about 1.5 acres) was also used for grants to Buddhist monks, who received 100 nivartanas.

st.2: Aditya I was the immediate successor of Vijayalaya.

x: Both statements are correct: Vijayalaya took Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars and was succeeded by Aditya I, the father of Parantaka I.

st.1: The Cholas lost the battle of Takkolam to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III.

x: Both statements are correct: the Cholas under Parantaka I lost at Takkolam (949) to Krishna III, and Rajendra II was crowned on the battlefield of Koppam.

st.2: Land measurement covered the whole empire.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Alauddin's measurement covered only a large belt around the Doab and Delhi, not the whole empire.

st.2: He arrived in India in 1333.
st.4: He noted that sati was completely prohibited in the Sultanate.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: born at Tangiers, he reached India in 1333 and was made Qazi of Delhi and envoy to China. Statement 4 is wrong: he noted that sati needed the Sultan's permission, not that it was banned.

st.3: Ibrahim Lodi was the son of Sikandar Lodi.

x: All three statements are correct: the Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty; Sikandar was Bahlol's son and Ibrahim was Sikandar's son.

st.2: Shah Abbas of Persia helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Humayun was helped by Shah Tahmasp of Persia, not Shah Abbas.

st.3: Sir Thomas Roe came as the ambassador of Charles I and stayed till 1619.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Roe (1615-19) was the ambassador of James I.

st.2: His first coronation came in 1658 after Samugarh and the second in 1659 after Deorai.

x: All three statements are correct: Alamgir was crowned in 1658 after Samugarh and again in 1659 after Deorai, and the Child's War was the first Mughal war with the English.

st.3: 'Sarvalokeshvara' was a title of the Kushana king Vima Kadphises.

x: All three statements are correct: Suraj Mal built Lohagarh, Sawai Jai Singh II built five observatories, and Sarvalokeshvara was a title of Vima Kadphises (Saadat Khan was Burhan-ul-Mulk).

st.4: John Fryer found that Hindu women of the Deccan moved about freely, unlike veiled Muslim women.

x: All four statements are correct; Fryer contrasted the free movement of Deccan Hindu women with the strict purdah of Muslim women.

st.3: His Sirr-i-Akbar is a Persian translation of the Bhagavad Gita.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Sirr-i-Akbar is a Persian translation of fifty Upanishads, not the Gita.

st.2: Forty-one of his shabdas are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

x: All three statements are correct: Ravidas, of a leather-tanner background, has 41 shabdas in the Guru Granth Sahib and dreamt of Begampura.

st.1: Potana wrote eight of its twelve skandhas.

x: All four statements are correct: Potana wrote 8 of the 12 skandhas, the 5th was by Bopparaju Gangana, the 6th by Erchuri Singana, and C.P. Brown printed it in 1840.

st.2: The Carnatic Trinity consists of Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Annamacharya.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Trinity is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri; Annamacharya was an earlier composer.

st.1: Chauth, one-fourth of the land revenue, was levied only on the Swaraj lands under direct Maratha rule.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: chauth (one-fourth) was levied on lands outside direct Maratha rule, not on the Swaraj.

st.2: By the Treaty of Doraha Sarai (1738) the Nizam ceded Malwa.

x: All three statements are correct: Mungi-Shevgaon followed Palkhed, Doraha Sarai (after Bhopal) gave the Marathas Malwa, and the Nizam blamed Shore's neutrality for Kharda.

st.2: Karl Marx called the revolt "in truth a national revolt" in the New-York Tribune.

x: All three statements are correct: Disraeli raised the question in the Commons, Marx wrote of a national revolt in the New-York Tribune, and Sir Syed blamed the absence of Indians in the Council.

st.2: Mir Qasim fought at Buxar as the reigning Nawab of Bengal.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Mir Qasim had been deposed in 1763 and Mir Jafar restored, so he fought at Buxar as the ousted Nawab.

st.4: He was Governor-General during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

x: All four statements are correct: the Cornwallis Code (1793), 'Father of Civil Services', death at Ghazipur in 1805, and the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92).

st.3: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 was passed during the viceroyalty of Lord Lansdowne.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1861 Act and the portfolio system came under Canning, and the 1892 Act under Lansdowne.

st.4: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was proposed by Col. Henry Atlock Lake and built under Charles Orr.

x: All four statements are correct: after the Guntur famine (1833) the Dowleswaram anicut was built (1846-52), Veenam Veeranna became Rao Bahadur, and the Krishna anicut was proposed by Lake and built by Orr.

st.2: The Kanpur (Cawnpore) Bolshevik conspiracy case (1924) was launched after the CPI had been founded at Kanpur.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kanpur case came in 1924, before the CPI conference at Kanpur in 1925.

st.3: Satyavadini (1905) was his reply to Kasibhatta's Arya Mata Bodhini.

x: All three statements are correct: Satihita Bodhini (1883) merged into Telugu Zenana in 1904, Satya Samvardhini came in 1891, and Satyavadini (1905) answered Arya Mata Bodhini (his reply to Hasyavardhini was Hasya Sanjeevani).

st.1: Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj at Calcutta in 1882.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Arya Mahila Samaj (1882) was founded at Pune; Calcutta is where she got the titles Pandita and Saraswati.

st.2: Lord Hardinge was killed in the attack.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Hardinge was only wounded.

st.3: The August Declaration of 20 August 1917 was made by the Viceroy Lord Chelmsford.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the August Declaration was made by the Secretary of State Edwin Montagu.

st.2: It was called off soon after the Police Action of September 1948.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the struggle went on after the Police Action and was called off only in October 1951.

st.2: L.C. Adami and D.J. Reid were among its members.
st.3: It recommended a 25 per cent refund of the illegal recoveries, which Gandhi rejected as too low.

st.2: About 25,000 satyagrahis had been convicted by May 1941.
st.4: It was suspended by the Congress Working Committee after the Cripps Mission's offer.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the CWC suspended it in December 1941, before the Cripps Mission (March 1942).

st.2: Lord Mountbatten's 'Breakdown Plan' of phased withdrawal to the Muslim provinces was put to the Cabinet Mission in 1946.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Breakdown Plan (1946) was Lord Wavell's, not Mountbatten's.

st.1: Its early English name was passive resistance, which Gandhi called the weapon of the weak, unlike satyagraha.

x: All three statements are correct: Gandhi called passive resistance the weapon of the weak and satyagraha that of the strongest; it rests on suffering and aims to change the opponent's heart.

x: All three items were part of the Kurnool Circular, which aimed to paralyse communications and administration; raids on British military camps were not in it.

st.2: Gopal Krishna Gokhale belonged to the Extremist group along with Tilak.
st.3: Bipin Chandra Pal was a Moderate leader.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Gokhale was a Moderate. Statement 3 is wrong: Bipin Chandra Pal was an Extremist (Lal-Bal-Pal).

st.2: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao led the first salt squad in Madras in 1930.

st.4: Mutnuri Krishna Rao invited Lala Lajpat Rai to Andhra in 1907.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Prakasam was municipal chairman of Rajahmundry. Statement 4 is wrong: Mutnuri invited Bipin Chandra Pal in 1907.

x: All three statements are correct: Banerji's 12 types, dolmens for elites and pits for commoners, and iron tools with black-and-red ware as grave goods.

st.3: The Bhattiprolu inscriptions are in Prakrit, written in a local variant of Brahmi.

x: All three statements are correct: Bhattiprolu has the oldest stupa relic caskets of Andhra, Roman coins, and Prakrit inscriptions in the Bhattiprolu variant of Brahmi.

st.2: His defeat at the hands of the Pallavas is recorded in the Manchikallu inscription of Simhavarman.

x: All three statements are correct: Rudrapurushadatta was defeated by Pallava Simhavarman (Manchikallu), not by the Vishnukundins, and his Nagarjunakonda pillar honours his mother Vammabhatta.

st.3: The Lilavati Parinayam, by Kutuhala, is written in Prakrit.

x: All three statements are correct: Sarvavarma's Katantra was a short Sanskrit grammar, and Kutuhala's Prakrit Lilavati Parinayam has Hala marry Lilavati at Draksharama.

st.1: Vijayapuri is thought to be named after the Satavahana king Vijaya Satakarni.

x: All three statements are correct: Vijayapuri is linked to Vijaya Satakarni, R. Subrahmanyam led the 1954–60 rescue dig, and Ghantasala and Motupalli were ports.

st.2: The Chola Rajadhiraja I was killed at Dharanikota by Ahavamalla Someshwara.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Rajadhiraja I was killed in the battle of Koppam (1054), not at Dharanikota.

st.2: The capital was shifted to Vengi (Pedavegi, near Eluru) by Jayasimha I (Vallabha).

x: All three statements are correct: Pithapuram under Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Vengi under Jayasimha I, and Rajamahendravaram under Ammaraja I.

st.4: Somarama is the only Pancharama on the Krishna.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Pancharama on the Krishna is Amararama at Amaravati; Somarama is at Gunupudi, Bhimavaram.

st.3: 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' occurs in Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada.
st.4: Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks the birth anniversary of Gurajada Apparao.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: 29 August is the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.

st.3: Kamban is known for the Tamil Ramayana, the Ramavataram.

x: All three statements are correct: Tamil was first to get classical status (2004), Tayumanavar was a Saiva saint-poet, and Kamban wrote the Tamil Ramayana.

st.3: Marco Polo later visited Motupalli during the reign of Rudramadevi.

x: All three statements are correct: Ganapatideva issued the Abhaya Sasanam in 1244 for the safety of sea merchants, and Marco Polo visited Motupalli under Rudramadevi.

st.2: After 1424 he joined the Rajahmundry court of Veerabhadra Reddi.

x: All four statements are correct: Srinatha won the Kanakabhishekam at Deva Raya II's court, joined Veerabhadra Reddi at Rajahmundry after 1424, was Kavi Sarvabhauma, and was poor in Palnadu after 1448.

st.2: Ahmad Shah I shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.

st.4: Udayagiri, their major stronghold in southern Andhra, is in the Krishna district.

st.3: Bidriware - a blackened zinc alloy inlaid with silver - developed under the Bahmani rulers of Bidar.

x: All three statements are correct: the Matsyas of Oddadi had the double-fish emblem, their founder married Jayatsena's daughter, and the Pusapati and Madgole zamindaris replaced them.

st.3: The Polavaram inscription names 14 members of the Musunuri lineage, of whom only three ruled.

x: All three statements are correct: Kapaya took Orugallu in 1336, his nephew Anapota governed Vengi, and the Polavaram inscription lists 14 members, only three of whom ruled.

st.2: The Recherla Velama kingdom is dated 1325-1475.

x: All four statements are correct: Musunuri 1325-1368, Reddi 1325-1448, Recherla Velama 1325-1475, and the childless Prolaya Nayaka was succeeded by his cousin Kapaya.

st.2: After the estate was seized in 1793, the Raja was told to live at Machilipatnam.
st.4: Narayana Babu, the brother of the slain Raja, was restored on paying the arrears.

st.2: Pal delivered five lectures at Rajahmundry.
st.4: The tour began at Rajahmundry.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the tour began at Vizianagaram.

st.3: Its leaders Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam were killed in July 1970.

st.2: Velugu, started in 2000 by Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu, was run by the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP).

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Section 87 said no Indian would be debarred from office by religion, birth, descent or colour. Statement 3 is wrong: the first Law Commission was headed by Lord Macaulay.

st.2: Bicameral legislatures were provided in six provinces, including Punjab.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the six bicameral provinces were Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces – not Punjab.

st.2: Its revocation needs the approval of Parliament.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the President may revoke President's Rule by a later proclamation without Parliament's approval.

st.1: In August 2026, the Centre backed an income-based creamy layer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: in August 2026 the Centre opposed an income-based creamy layer for SCs and STs.

st.2: Before 1950, only the Calcutta, Bombay and Allahabad High Courts could issue writs.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: before 1950 only the Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts could issue writs.

st.2: Article 51A(e) uses the word 'fraternity', exactly as the Preamble does.
st.3: Under Article 51A(a), citizens must protect the National Flag.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 51A(e) speaks of the spirit of common 'brotherhood'. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 51A(a) asks citizens to respect the National Flag and Anthem.

st.3: The tenure of the President requires ratification.
st.4: The States must ratify within six months.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it is the election of the President and its manner that needs ratification, not his tenure. Statement 4 is wrong: the Constitution fixes no time limit for ratification.

st.2: The 74th Amendment applies only to some specified States.
st.3: The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Municipalities.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 74th Amendment applies to all States, with a few exempted areas. Statement 3 is wrong: Municipalities got constitutional status from the 74th Amendment; the 73rd covers Panchayats.

st.2: Under Article 243ZJ, a co-operative board may have a maximum of 21 directors, and no member may be co-opted to it.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the board may have up to 21 directors and may also co-opt two members with expertise.

st.2: In counting the six-month period, only periods of prorogation are excluded, not periods of adjournment.
st.3: Failure of the other House to return the Bill within 14 days is a ground for a joint sitting.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: periods of prorogation or of adjournment for more than four consecutive days are both excluded. Statement 3 is wrong: the ground is more than six months passing without the Bill being passed; 14 days relates to Money Bills.

st.1: Unsoundness of mind disqualifies even without a declaration by a competent court.
st.3: The term 'office of profit' is defined in the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: unsoundness of mind disqualifies only if declared by a competent court. Statement 3 is wrong: 'office of profit' is defined neither in the Constitution nor in the RP Act.

st.2: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, to raise the Lok Sabha's maximum from 550 to 850, was passed by the Lok Sabha.
st.4: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolved to raise the Lok Sabha to 850 seats.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 131st Amendment Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha, short of the special majority. Statement 4 is wrong: Tamil Nadu resolved to keep the Lok Sabha at 543.

st.1: The salaries of the Prime Minister and Union Ministers are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
st.2: The salaries and expenses of the Election Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the salaries of the PM and Ministers are voted, not charged. Statement 2 is wrong: the Election Commission's salaries and expenses are also voted.

st.3: In the 17th Lok Sabha, no Bill was passed within two weeks of its introduction.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in the 17th Lok Sabha, 58 per cent of Bills were passed within two weeks of introduction.

st.3: 5 members are elected by teachers of primary schools and above.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 5 teachers' members are elected by teachers of secondary schools and above, not primary.

st.1: The American President has an absolute veto, which the Indian President does not.
st.3: As in the USA, the Indian President must decide on a Bill within 10 days, failing which it becomes law.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it is the Indian President who has an absolute veto; the American President's veto is qualified. Statement 3 is wrong: the Indian President has no time limit, hence the pocket veto.

st.2: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to both Houses of Parliament.
st.4: A person who is not a Member of Parliament cannot be appointed a Minister at all.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha only. Statement 4 is wrong: a non-member can be a Minister for up to six months.

st.1: Under Article 233, 'district judge' includes an additional district judge and a chief presidency magistrate.
st.2: The All India Judicial Service, enabled by Article 312, has been constituted.
st.4: A person directly recruited as a district judge is appointed by the Governor without consulting the High Court.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the definition of 'district judge' is in Article 236. Statement 2 is wrong: the AIJS has not yet been constituted. Statement 4 is wrong: the Governor appoints district judges in consultation with the High Court.

st.1: Article 21 uses the expression 'due process of law' and not 'procedure established by law'.
st.3: In Kishorchandra Chhanganlal Rathod (2024) the Supreme Court held delimitation orders wholly immune from judicial review.
st.4: The 42nd Amendment reversed the 38th Amendment's bar on reviewing the President's satisfaction.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 21 uses 'procedure established by law'. Statement 3 is wrong: the Court held delimitation orders open to review if manifestly arbitrary. Statement 4 is wrong: it was the 44th Amendment that reversed the 38th.

st.2: Its members have a five-year term and are eligible for reappointment.
st.3: The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 is one of the seven Acts in Schedule I of the NGT Act.
st.4: An appeal against its order lies to the High Court within 90 days.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NGT members serve five years and are not eligible for reappointment. Statement 3 is wrong: the Wild Life Act is not in Schedule I. Statement 4 is wrong: the appeal lies to the Supreme Court.

st.2: The 80th Amendment folded surcharges on Union taxes into the Article 270 pool.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: surcharges and cesses stay outside the divisible pool.

st.3: It used the population of both 1971 and 2011.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 15th Finance Commission used only the 2011 population, adding demographic performance to reward States.

st.3: According to the AP Finance Minister, the 16th Finance Commission raised AP's revenue-deficit grants.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th Finance Commission dropped revenue-deficit grants, and AP says it lost up to ₹38,000 crore.

st.1: Article 148(4) allows the CAG to take further office under the Government with the President's approval.
st.3: The Constitution debars retiring Election Commissioners from any further appointment by the Government.
st.4: The expenses of the Election Commission of India are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 148(4) bars the CAG from any further office under the Government. Statement 3 is wrong: the Constitution does not bar Election Commissioners from later appointments. Statement 4 is wrong: the Election Commission's expenses are voted, not charged.

st.2: When a poll adjourned under Section 57 resumes, all voters on the roll may vote again.
st.3: Under Section 58A, the ECI may declare a poll void if an EVM is unlawfully taken away or tampered with.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only those who did not vote earlier may vote at the resumed poll. Statement 3 is wrong: EVM tampering falls under Section 58; Section 58A deals with booth capturing.

st.2: A member submits his resignation to the Governor of the State concerned.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a member of a Joint SPSC resigns to the President, who appoints him.

st.2: After 2014, reports on the accounts of undivided Andhra Pradesh went only to the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: reports on undivided AP went to the Governors of both AP and Telangana.

st.2: The Commission can impose criminal sentences on persons who violate the rights of women.
st.3: 'Mahila Jan Sunwai' is a public hearing of women's grievances organised by the National Human Rights Commission.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCW is a recommendatory body and cannot punish anyone. Statement 3 is wrong: Mahila Jan Sunwai is organised by the NCW, not the NHRC.
Both statements are correct: insolvency and similar grounds allow direct removal by the President, while misbehaviour or incapacity needs a Supreme Court inquiry on his reference.

st.1: Justice J.S. Verma was the first NHRC Chairperson.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first NHRC Chairperson was Justice Ranganath Misra (1993-96).

st.1: The Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809, and Britain was the first Commonwealth country to adopt it.
st.3: The world's first right-to-information law was enacted by New Zealand in 1962.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: New Zealand (1962) was the first Commonwealth country with an Ombudsman; Britain followed in 1967. Statement 3 is wrong: the first RTI law was Sweden's of 1766.

st.2: An integrated judiciary is a federal feature of the Constitution.
st.3: The division of powers between the Union and the States is a unitary feature of the Constitution.
st.4: The Sarkaria Commission on Union-State relations was set up by the Janata government.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: an integrated judiciary is a unitary feature. Statement 3 is wrong: division of powers is a federal feature. Statement 4 is wrong: the Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 by Indira Gandhi's Congress government.

st.3: It recommended that residuary powers be vested in the Concurrent List.
st.4: It proposed transferring foreign affairs to the State List.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajamannar wanted residuary powers given to the States. Statement 4 is wrong: it proposed moving subjects like stock exchanges and trade unions, not foreign affairs.

st.1: Electoral rolls have four qualifying dates, one of which is 1 December.
st.3: A candidate's election expense account must be filed with the Chief Electoral Officer of the State.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. Statement 3 is wrong: the account is filed with the District Election Officer.

st.1: The Village/Ward Secretariats launched on 2 October 2019 replaced the Gram Panchayats as the unit of rural administration.
st.2: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 2 October.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Secretariats work alongside the Gram Panchayats and did not replace them. Statement 2 is wrong: National Panchayati Raj Day is 24 April.

st.2: Viability Gap Funding is a grant for PPP projects that are commercially viable.
st.3: Under VGF, the Centre alone bears the whole viability gap, the sponsoring authority contributing nothing.
st.4: The NIIF is wholly owned by the Centre, with no foreign investors.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: VGF is for projects that are economically justified but commercially unviable. Statement 3 is wrong: the Centre normally gives 20% and the sponsoring authority 20% (30% + 30% in the social sector). Statement 4 is wrong: the Centre holds 49% of NIIF, the rest coming from domestic and foreign investors.

st.1: MeeSeva single-window G2C service centres were launched in 2011 under Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: MeeSeva was launched in 2011 under Chief Minister N. Kiran Kumar Reddy.

st.1: Its implementation in government departments was begun by the Planning Commission.
st.4: Sevottam-compliant certification follows IS 15700:2005, issued by the Quality Council of India.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Sevottam is a DARPG model. Statement 4 is wrong: IS 15700:2005 is a standard of the Bureau of Indian Standards.

st.1: The National Centre for Good Governance was upgraded from the National Institute of Administrative Research; its head office is in Mussoorie and branch in New Delhi.
st.3: Telangana's Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance platform offers over 500 services.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NCGG head office is in New Delhi, with a branch at Mussoorie. Statement 3 is wrong: Mana Mitra is Andhra Pradesh's platform.

st.2: It can impose a penalty of up to ₹250 crore as well as imprisonment.
st.4: The DPDP Act, 2023 left the RTI Act untouched.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Board can impose only monetary penalties, not imprisonment. Statement 4 is wrong: the DPDP Act amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act.

st.2: The Regulatory Reform Bill, 2013 for infrastructure regulators was drafted by the Law Commission.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Regulatory Reform Bill, 2013 was drafted by the Planning Commission.

st.2: India owes allegiance to the British Crown as a member of the Commonwealth.
st.3: India has never hosted CHOGM.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India accepts the Crown only as the symbol and Head of the Commonwealth, with no allegiance. Statement 3 is wrong: India hosted CHOGM at New Delhi in 1983.

st.3: Coastal Andhra accounts for about 64% of its area.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Rayalaseema, not Coastal Andhra, accounts for about 64% of the APMIP area.

st.3: KWDT-II, chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar, gave its award in 2010 and it has been notified.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the KWDT-II award has not been notified; it is under challenge in the Supreme Court.

st.2: Royalty on onshore oil and natural gas accrues to the Union Government.
st.3: Power of the Central Generating Stations was divided in the population ratio of 58.32 : 41.68.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: onshore royalty goes to the producing State. Statement 3 is wrong: CGS power was split by the last five years' consumption (AP about 46%), not the population ratio.

st.1: The LEADS index was introduced by DPIIT in 2018.

x: All three statements are correct: LEADS (DPIIT, 2018), ULIP – Unified Logistics Interface Platform, and the NLP aim of single-digit logistics cost by 2030.

st.3: It was signed at Geneva.

x: All three statements are correct: the GATT was signed at Geneva on 30 October 1947 by 23 contracting parties; Marrakesh (1994) created the WTO.

st.2: The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019 because the USA blocked appointments.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India has not joined the EU-led MPIA. (The Appellate Body has indeed been non-functional since December 2019 because the USA blocked appointments.)

st.3: The gap between male and female literacy was largest in Rajasthan and smallest in Meghalaya.

x: All three statements are correct: final literacy 72.98%, Lakshadweep highest among UTs, and the gender gap largest in Rajasthan and smallest in Meghalaya.

st.3: It removes the two-child norm for local body elections.

x: All four statements are correct: the draft moves to population management, offers ₹25,000 for a second or third child, drops the two-child norm for local body polls, and Kshema covers elderly care.

st.4: Class III towns recorded the highest growth in Census 2001.

x: All four statements are correct: the 1981 criteria are kept, MoHUA objected before the Magunta committee, 468 Class I towns held about 70% in 2011, and Class III towns grew fastest in 2001.

st.2: Women must form at least one-half of the beneficiaries.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: women must be at least one-third of the beneficiaries, not one-half.

st.3: Vahana Mitra was one of its pillars.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Vahana Mitra was a separate scheme, not one of the nine Navaratnalu.

st.3: Under Section 108, the President could issue orders to remove difficulties within three years.

x: All three statements are correct: Section 46 on the Finance Commission awards, Section 66 references within three years, and Section 108 orders within three years.

st.2: The Indian Statistical Institute is an attached office of MoSPI with no statutory basis.
st.3: The National Statistical Office follows the IMF's General Data Dissemination System (GDDS).

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ISI is an autonomous body under the ISI Act, 1959. Statement 3 is wrong: the NSO follows the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS).

st.1: AP's unemployment rate was below the national rate, thanks to low urban unemployment.
st.3: AP's youth (15-29) unemployment rate was lower than India's.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's rate (4.1%) was above India's (3.2%), driven by urban and youth unemployment. Statement 3 is wrong: AP's youth rate (17.5%) was well above India's (10.2%).

st.1: It was 32.5% in 2020-21 and has fallen in every round since.
st.3: In 2025 the urban female LFPR (about 45.9%) was higher than the rural female LFPR (about 27.7%).

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: from 32.5% in 2020-21 it rose to 41.7% in 2023-24. Statement 3 is wrong: in 2025 the rural female LFPR (about 45.9%) was higher than the urban (about 27.7%).

st.2: The unorganised sector employs less than half of all workers but generates over 80% of output.
st.3: The inter-state Gini coefficient of per capita income fell from 0.261 in 1994-95 to 0.230.
st.4: In 2024-25 Andhra Pradesh's per capita income was higher than Telangana's.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the unorganised sector employs over 80% of workers but yields only about 45% of output. Statement 3 is wrong: the Gini rose from 0.230 to 0.261, so imbalance widened. Statement 4 is wrong: Telangana's per capita income was about 1.35 times AP's.

st.1: Foreign exchange reserves were enough to pay for more than a year of imports.
st.3: It was caused by the East Asian financial crisis.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: reserves covered only about two weeks of imports. Statement 3 is wrong: the East Asian crisis came in 1997; the 1991 crisis came from fiscal and current-account deficits and the Gulf War oil shock.

st.3: Wildlife conservation and renewable energy production are human-driven causes of environmental degradation.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: wildlife conservation and renewable energy reduce degradation; they are not causes of it.

st.2: AP's poverty ratio under the Lakdawala method was 44.6% in 1993-94.
st.3: AP's poverty ratio under the Tendulkar method was 15.8% in 2004-05.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 44.6% (1993-94) is the Tendulkar figure, not Lakdawala's. Statement 3 is wrong: 15.8% for 2004-05 is the old official (URP) estimate; the Tendulkar figure is 29.9%.

st.3: The Planning and Development Department (1944) was headed by John Mathai.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Planning and Development Department was headed by Ardeshir Dalal.

st.4: Under the 16th FC, AP's share fell from 4.217% to 4.047%.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: under the 16th FC AP's share rose, from 4.047% to 4.217%.

st.3: In the SDG India Index 2023-24 both AP's composite score and its rank improved over 2020-21.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AP's score rose (72 to 74) but its rank fell (4th to 9th).

st.2: Withdrawal of accommodation signals an easing bias, with liquidity being added.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: withdrawal of accommodation signals a tightening bias, with surplus liquidity being drained.

st.1: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement of 20 February 2015 is a statute enacted by Parliament.
st.3: Section 45ZB of the RBI Act deals with the inflation target and Section 45ZA with the Monetary Policy Committee.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the MPFA is an agreement between the Government and the RBI, not a statute. Statement 3 is wrong: Section 45ZA deals with the inflation target and Section 45ZB with the MPC.

st.1: Government health spending is 1.43% of GDP, already above the NHP 2017 target.
st.2: The health share of total government spending rose from 4.89% in 2021-22 to 6.12% in 2022-23.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 1.43% of GDP is well below the NHP 2017 target of 2.5%. Statement 2 is wrong: the health share fell, from 6.12% in 2021-22 to 4.89% in 2022-23.

st.1: Dr Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Bank and Andhra Insurance Co. (1925) and defeated Subhas Chandra Bose in the 1939 Congress presidential election.
st.2: Lala Lajpat Rai was among the founders of Canara Bank.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Bose defeated Pattabhi in 1939; Pattabhi became INC President in 1948-49. Statement 2 is wrong: Lala Lajpat Rai was linked to Punjab National Bank; Canara Bank was founded by Ammembal Subba Rao Pai.

st.1: Basel I (1988) covered credit, market and operational risk, with minimum capital at 8% of risk-weighted assets.
st.3: India began implementing Basel III norms in 1999, with a CRAR of 9%.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Basel I covered only credit risk, with five risk buckets. Statement 3 is wrong: 1999 (CRAR 9%) was India's adoption of Basel I; Basel III began in India from 1 January 2013.

st.2: Interest on an NPA is booked as income when it falls due.
st.3: Provision Coverage Ratio = provisions held ÷ gross NPAs; a higher PCR indicates a weaker bank.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: interest on an NPA is booked only when actually received. Statement 3 is wrong: a higher PCR shows a more resilient bank.

st.2: Under the Inter-Creditor Agreement of July 2018, a resolution plan approved by the lead bank alone binds all lenders.
st.3: The RBI's Prudential Framework of 7 June 2019 made the ICA optional and set a 30-day review period.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under the ICA a plan binds all lenders once lenders holding 66% approve. Statement 3 is wrong: the Prudential Framework made the ICA mandatory.

st.2: State Excise is the largest source of Andhra Pradesh's own-tax revenue in 2024-25 (RE).

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SGST (38%) is AP's largest own-tax source; State Excise (22%) comes second.

st.2: The securities transaction tax is an indirect tax because it is collected by the stock exchange.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: STT is a direct tax, falling on the investor who trades.

st.2: Pulses are India's largest import item.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: crude petroleum is India's largest import item, not pulses.

st.2: Maharashtra was the first Indian State to issue one, in 2019.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kerala (through KIIFB, 2019) was the first State to issue a masala bond.

st.2: Section 16 provides for a single National Food Commission for all the States.
st.4: The central issue prices of ₹3/₹2/₹1 have been revised upward every year since 2013.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Section 16 provides for a State Food Commission in every State. Statement 4 is wrong: the issue prices have not been revised since July 2013.

st.2: During FY16-FY25 the crop sector grew faster than fisheries and livestock.
st.3: Agriculture and allied growth turned negative in FY26.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: crops grew 3.5% against fisheries 8.8% and livestock 7.1%. Statement 3 is wrong: provisional FY26 growth was a positive 3.0%.

st.2: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by the Ministry of Rural Development.
st.3: The committee that drafted the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act was headed by M.S. Swaminathan.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Model Act was prepared by NITI Aayog. Statement 3 is wrong: the drafting committee was headed by T. Haque.

st.1: The Union Budget 2018-19 proposed converting 22,000 APMC mandis into Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs).
st.2: The Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund was meant only for APMC mandis, not for GrAMs.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 22,000 to be upgraded were rural haats, not APMC mandis. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rs 2,000 crore Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund was set up for GrAMs as well as APMCs.
Both statements are correct: TPDS and Decentralised Procurement came in 1997, and the Revamped PDS in 1992.

st.1: It places CPSEs in four schedules, but Ratna status is granted by NITI Aayog.
st.2: Since July 2021, it has been under the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the DPE itself grants Ratna status. Statement 2 is wrong: since July 2021 the DPE is under the Ministry of Finance.

st.1: They have been treated as a priority only since the Second Plan.
st.2: They are capital-intensive and need much capital per worker, so they generate little employment.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: they have been a priority since the First Plan. Statement 2 is wrong: they are labour-intensive with low capital per worker and so generate large employment.
All three statements are correct: the 16th Finance Commission under Arvind Panagariya kept the States' share at 41%, though eighteen States had sought 50%.

st.2: In a regulated market yard, the farmer sells directly to the consumer.
st.3: Rythu Bazars are run by the Agricultural Market Committees under the 1966 Act.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: direct farmer-to-consumer sale is the Rythu Bazar model; regulated yards sell through traders and commission agents. Statement 3 is wrong: Rythu Bazars are outside the purview of the AMCs, run by an Estate Officer.

st.3: The Electronics Manufacturing Policy (4.0) focuses on a single cluster at Visakhapatnam.
st.4: The Tourism Policy (March 2026) offering a 5-10% FCI subsidy was issued by the Union Ministry of Tourism.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Electronics (4.0) policy focuses on clusters at Kopparthy, Tirupati and Sri City. Statement 4 is wrong: the Tourism Policy of March 2026 is Andhra Pradesh's, with a subsidy up to Rs 40 crore.

st.1: The AP Cluster Development Programme 2026-30 is a Central scheme of the Union MSME Ministry.
st.3: APSES 2024-25 counts 1,074 operational large and mega units, all of them in the public sector.
st.4: In June 2026 the Cabinet rejected 87 SIPB projects.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Cluster Development Programme 2026-30 is AP's own (45 clusters, up to 80% of cost). Statement 3 is wrong: the 1,074 units (5.33 lakh jobs) are mostly private. Statement 4 is wrong: the Cabinet ratified the 87 projects (Rs 34,000 crore).

st.3: The AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026 amends the APEDB Act, 2018.
st.4: The Single Desk Portal is a Government-to-Citizen (G2C) platform.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Omnibus Bill amends the Single Window Clearance Act, 2002. Statement 4 is wrong: the Single Desk Portal is a G2B platform for investors.

st.3: BHAVYA (Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana, 2026) provides for plug-and-play industrial parks only in the North-Eastern States.
st.4: BHAVYA is to be funded wholly by private investors, with no Central outlay.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: BHAVYA provides for 100 plug-and-play parks across the country. Statement 4 is wrong: BHAVYA has a Central outlay of ₹33,660 crore.

st.1: It was taken up under the Sagarmala programme and is a priority link of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
st.2: It starts at Devanahalli in Karnataka.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the expressway is under Bharatmala Phase-I, not Sagarmala. Statement 2 is wrong: it starts at Hoskote.

st.1: It replaced the Indian Electricity Act 1910, the Electricity (Supply) Act 1948 and the Energy Conservation Act 2001.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the third Act replaced was the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act 1998; the Energy Conservation Act 2001 remains.

st.2: India's nuclear reactors are operated by NTPC.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India's nuclear reactors are run by NPCIL.

st.3: Of the 100 GW target set in 2015, the larger share was earmarked for rooftop solar.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: only 40 GW was for rooftop; the larger 60 GW was for large and medium grid-connected plants.

st.2: The first EIA notification was issued in 1994 under the Water Act and revised in 2006.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1994 EIA notification was issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, not the Water Act.

st.3: A place 30° west of Greenwich is 2 hours behind GMT.

x: All three statements are correct: 1° = 4 minutes, so 1′ = 4 seconds and 15° = 1 hour; places west of Greenwich are behind GMT.

st.3: Clay holds more water because its pore spaces are large.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: clay holds more water because its pores are very small and its surface area large.
